definitions.A_star_t: sup_{x in R^3,r>0} r^(-1) integral_{B(x,r)} |u(y,t)|^2 dy

assumptions.solution: u is a bounded mild ancient solution of 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes on R^3 x (-infinity,0), hence smooth at every t<0.

derivative_loss_circularity_audit.circular_bootstrap: No regularity criterion is assumed to prove the Hodge-Morrey lemma or global near-max consequence. Existing regularity criteria are consumer-signature checks only.
derivative_loss_circularity_audit.derivative_loss: No derivative beyond the already source-bound R6 K_star estimate is introduced. The Hodge kernel gains one derivative from omega to u locally plus a harmonic remainder.
derivative_loss_circularity_audit.numerics: NONE; no numerical evidence is used for theorem authority.

global_consequence.near_global_vorticity_times: For any theta in (0,1) and any t with Omega_t>=theta Omega_star, chi_t:=K_t/Omega_t^2 satisfies chi_t <= C I theta^(-2). Such times exist arbitrarily close to the vorticity supremum by the definition of Omega_star when Omega_star>0.
global_consequence.statement: Taking the supremum over t gives M_star <= C I^(1/4) Omega_star^(1/2). Combining with the inherited R6 bound K_star<=C M_star^4 gives K_star <= C I Omega_star^2.
global_consequence.trivial_branch: If Omega_star=0, the local Hodge-Morrey estimate gives M_star=0 and u=0.

lemma.constants: C is universal up to the fixed cutoff profile and dimension; no numerical threshold is used.
endpoint_checks: no Lorentz/BMO endpoint embedding is invoked
proof: Choose eta in C_c^infty(B(x0,r)), eta=1 on B(x0,3r/4), with standard scale-r derivative bounds.
Let v=curl(-Delta)^(-1)(eta omega). Its kernel has size C|x-y|^(-2), hence ||v||_{L^infty(B(x0,r/2))} <= C r Omega_t and ||v||_{L^2(B(x0,r/2))} <= C r^(5/2) Omega_t.
Because div u=0, -Delta u=curl omega. On B(x0,r/2), eta=1 and grad eta=0, so -Delta v=curl omega there. Thus h=u-v is harmonic on B(x0,r/2).
The harmonic interior L2-to-pointwise estimate gives |h(x0)| <= C r^(-3/2)||h||_{L^2(B(x0,r/2))}. Combining with the bound on v yields |u(x0)| <= C[r^(-3/2)||u||_{L^2(B(x0,r))}+r Omega_t].
A_star_t<=I gives |u(x0)| <= C[I^(1/2)r^(-1)+Omega_t r]. For Omega_t>0 optimize at r=I^(1/4)Omega_t^(-1/2). If Omega_t=0, let r->infinity and obtain u(t)=0. This yields M_t<=C I^(1/4)Omega_t^(1/2).
lemma.scaling_check: Under u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), I and A_star are invariant, M_t scales as lambda, Omega_t as lambda^2; I^(1/4)Omega_t^(1/2) scales as lambda.
lemma.statement: For every fixed t<0, x0 in R^3 and r>0, |u(x0,t)| <= C[r^(-3/2)||u(t)||_{L^2(B(x0,r))} + r Omega_t]. Consequently M_t <= C I^(1/4) Omega_t^(1/2).

pressure_nonlocality_audit.not_used: No pressure D term, local-energy flux sign, no-incoming theorem, ancestry information, or pressure cancellation is used.
pressure_nonlocality_audit.scope: Pressure/nonlocality remains an open possible repair coordinate and is not declared irrelevant.
pressure_nonlocality_audit.used: The new lemma uses only divergence-free Hodge structure, the finite-I A carrier, and vorticity amplitude.

quantifier_audit.anticipated_uniform_implication: finite I => chi_t<=C I for every t
quantifier_audit.first_exact_defect: The inherited ancient smoothing estimate is K_star<=C M_star^4. The local Hodge lemma controls M_t by Omega_t at each time, and M_star by Omega_star globally; it does not control M_star by the vorticity Omega_t at an arbitrary prescribed time. Therefore K_t/Omega_t^2 <= C I (Omega_star/Omega_t)^2, not C I uniformly unless Omega_t is known comparable to Omega_star.
quantifier_audit.not_claimed: No target-domain counterexample is known; the failure is a missing/invalid inference from the registered estimates, not a proof that actual NSE dynamics cannot provide record-time or ancestry alignment.

r7_reaudit.near_max_substitution: At Omega_t>=theta Omega_star this becomes <= C I/[a^2 min(a^2,c theta^2/I)]. In the derivative-limited regime the available sufficient bound is O(I^2 theta^(-2) a^(-2)).
r7_reaudit.producer_formula: At radius R=a Omega_t^(-1/2), R7 gives half-maximal vorticity volume fraction <= C I/[a^2 min(a^2,1/chi_t)].
r7_reaudit.remaining_scale_obstruction: A fixed small volume fraction is guaranteed by this estimate only at an a depending on I (and theta), whereas the audited Grujic vorticity consumer uses local one-dimensional sparseness at an absolute O(1) multiple of Omega_t^(-1/2). Arbitrary finite I therefore still does not source-bind the consumer scale.
r7_reaudit.remaining_type_obstruction: Volumetric sparsity is not identified with the required one-dimensional line sparseness.

residual_after: The same-source Hodge/Morrey lemma removes velocity-vorticity amplitude misalignment globally and collapses chi to O(I) on near-global-vorticity times, but arbitrary consumer times retain the ratio Omega_star/Omega_t; even at near-max times the sufficient sparsity radius remains I-dependent and geometry remains volumetric rather than one-dimensional.
residual_before: Independent finite-I and instantaneous chi(t) coordinates obstruct critical-scale geometric consumer glue.

source_carriers.ancient_smoothing_inherited_from_R6: K_star <= C M_star^4, with universal/source constant C; this is a global-in-time bound using M_star, not an instantaneous K_t<=C M_t^4 statement.
source_carriers.finite_I_time_slice: For each fixed smooth t<0 and each x,r, choose a parabolic ball contained in R^3 x R_- whose time interval contains t. Since A(Q)<=I and u is continuous in time, A_star_t<=I.
